summary.text: FLEX-2 is a microgravity droplet combustion investigation that aims to extend FLEX-1 results to fuels and conditions resembling real combustors, including bi-component fuel droplets.

fuels.text: Bi-component fuel droplets are a stated focus.

oxygen.text: Chamber O2 concentration varied between 0.1 and 0.4 mole fraction, with diluent gas as the balance.

pressure.text: Chamber pressure varied between 0.5 atm and 3.0 atm.

flow.text: Droplet translation velocity (and acceleration) is listed as an independently varied parameter.

gravity.text: Experiments are conducted in a microgravity environment, where buoyancy effects are minimized.

measurements.text: High speed photography tracks flame evolution; chamber pressure and temperature data were recorded.

hardware.text: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) and Multi-user Droplet Combustion Appartatus (MDCA).

claims.text: The investigation aims to extend FLEX-1 results to fuels and environmental conditions that mimic real combustor conditions.
The investigation aims to study flame extinction mechanisms and their boundaries.
The investigation aims to investigate the role of liquid-phase mixing on the burning characteristics of bi-component fuel droplets.
The investigation aims to provide benchmark experimental data on bi-component droplet combustion over a wide range of initial conditions to validate numerical simulations.
The investigation hypothesizes that conducting experiments in microgravity, where buoyancy effects are minimized, allows clearer observation of fundamental combustion processes.

limitations.text: This draft cites PSI metadata and no PDF text. The packet also includes official table passages whose findings have not been incorporated or reviewed.

modeling_resources.description: An experimental table file may document test parameters; the metadata lists the independently varied parameters including pressure and O2 concentration. No model is claimed to exist or be validated.
